issues.description: The problem specification contains an internal contradiction about the collection type used for Farm.animals: the UML diagram labels the attribute as List<Animal>, while the textual instructions in Part 3 explicitly require a Set implemented with a HashSet. This conflicting guidance can confuse students about whether they should implement a List or a Set for the Farm's animals and which behavior (allowing duplicates vs. enforcing uniqueness) is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across the specification: update the UML and any attribute mentions to match the textual requirement (Set<Animal> / HashSet) if uniqueness is intended, or change the textual instruction to List<Animal> if duplicates should be allowed. Preferably keep the textual instruction requiring a HashSet and change the UML attribute to animals: Set<Animal> to remove ambiguity.

issues.description: The provided reference solution implements Farm.animals as a List<Animal> (ArrayList) while the problem text requires using a Set implemented as a HashSet to ensure unique animals. This mismatch between the solution and the problem requirements could mislead students and cause grading/tests to expect different behavior (duplicates allowed vs. prevented).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the reference solution with the problem requirement by changing the Farm implementation to use Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>() (with appropriate imports), updating getter/setter signatures accordingly, and ensuring addAnimal uses the Set API. Alternatively, if the solution's List-based approach is intended, update the problem text to remove the HashSet/Set requirement and clarify that duplicates are allowed.

issues.description: The collection type used to hold animals is inconsistent across artifacts: the UML in the problem statement shows animals: List<Animal>, the textual requirement in the problem statement explicitly requires a Set implemented via HashSet, the template Farm.java leaves the collection unspecified (TODO), and the solution implements a List (ArrayList). This creates confusion for students about which collection type they must use (List vs Set/HashSet) and whether uniqueness (no duplicates) must be enforced by using a Set.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single collection type and make all artifacts consistent. Prefer matching the textual requirement: declare the field as private Set<Animal> animals; import java.util.Set and java.util.HashSet; initialize animals = new HashSet<>(); update getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal> and ensure addAnimal(Animal) adds to the Set. Alternatively, if List is intended, update the problem statement (both UML and text) to specify List/ArrayList and remove the requirement about HashSet and uniqueness.
